memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You must not do as they do in Egypt, where you used to live, and you must not do as they do in the land of Canaan, where I am bringing you. Do not follow their practices.'" - Lev 18:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Behind them, Egypt. Ahead of them, Canaan. And God says: do not live like either one.

Israel is caught between two cultures. The one they had absorbed for four hundred years, and the one they were about to move into. Both were normal to the people who lived in them. Both were about to be off-limits.

That is a picture of the Christian life. There is the culture we came out of — the assumptions we absorbed before we knew Christ, the reflexes still running in the background. And there is the culture we live in now, which shapes us constantly whether we notice it or not.

God's people have always been called to a certain kind of difference. Do not conform to the pattern of this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind (Rom 12:2). Not withdrawal — Israel was going to live in Canaan, and Jesus prayed that His followers would remain in the world (John 17:15). But not absorption either.

The hardest part is that culture is invisible from inside it. Israel would not have thought of Egyptian practices as "Egyptian." They would have thought of them as normal.

That is why we need Scripture. It shows us what we cannot see about ourselves.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What have you absorbed from your culture without ever examining it?
2. What did you bring from your life before Christ that still shapes you?
3. How can Scripture help you see what feels invisible?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I cannot see my own culture clearly from inside it. Use Your Word to show me where I have simply absorbed what is around me, and transform my thinking. Amen.
